findings.name: Page title
findings.evidence: head title count: 1; "Example Domain" (14 characters). 30–60 characters is a display heuristic, not a Google requirement.
findings.impact: A descriptive unique title helps readers and search tools identify the page.
findings.fix: Review whether the title clearly describes the page. Aim around 30–60 characters where natural; length alone does not predict ranking.

findings.name: Meta description
findings.evidence: meta[name=description] count: 0; "" (0 characters). 70–160 characters is a heuristic; search snippets are not guaranteed.
findings.impact: A clear summary can help tools describe this page; displayed snippets may differ.
findings.fix: Add one unique <meta name="description" content="…"> in <head>.

findings.name: Heading structure
findings.evidence: 0 DOM headings; H1 count 0; skipped levels false; empty headings false. []
findings.impact: Headings help readers and extraction tools follow the content hierarchy.
findings.fix: Use one clear H1 and ordered H2/H3 sections without skipping levels.

findings.name: Canonical URL
findings.impact: An unambiguous canonical can help consolidate duplicate page signals.
findings.fix: Add one absolute HTTPS <link rel="canonical" href="…"> in <head>, pointing to your preferred public page.

findings.name: Robots directives
findings.evidence: No robots meta found in DOM; X-Robots-Tag absent in retrieved main-document response. Default crawler behavior may apply; indexing not verified.
findings.impact: Noindex/nofollow directives affect crawler treatment when honored; indexing itself is unmeasured.
findings.fix: Review meta robots and X-Robots-Tag; remove restrictive directives only if this page should be discoverable.

findings.name: Image alt text
findings.evidence: 0 DOM img elements; missing alt: 0; explicit empty alt: 0. []. No img elements; other image forms unmeasured.
findings.impact: Useful alt text gives image meaning to screen readers and text extraction tools.
findings.fix: Add concise purpose-based alt text to informative images; keep alt="" only for decorative images.

findings.name: Open Graph metadata
findings.evidence: {"title":"","description":"","type":"","image":""}. Missing fields: title, description, type, image. Image URL syntax safe: true; image not downloaded.
findings.impact: Social and AI tools may use metadata for a consistent page summary.
findings.fix: Set og:title, og:description, og:type and a public absolute HTTPS og:image in <head>.

findings.name: Structured data
findings.evidence: 0 JSON-LD blocks; no parse errors; no basic shape warnings; types []; 0 microdata/RDFa candidate elements (not parsed). Syntax and basic presence only; schema semantics and rich-result eligibility not tested.
findings.impact: Machine-readable entities can help tools understand content. Presence does not guarantee rich results.
findings.fix: Add page-appropriate JSON-LD with @context and @type; validate syntax and review schema.org semantics separately.

findings.name: HTTP status
findings.evidence: Actual TinyFish Browser main-document GET status 200; final URL https://example.com/; redirects [].
findings.impact: Successful HTTP responses let tools retrieve content.
findings.fix: Return a successful public main-document response; investigate observed errors or unintended redirects.

findings.name: robots.txt policy
findings.evidence: Actually retrieved https://example.com/robots.txt; HTTP 404; no text response. Local policy result allowed (wildcard/PageProof/TinyFish groups).
findings.impact: Crawler restrictions may prevent tool access; policy does not prove indexing.
findings.fix: Review robots.txt rules with the site owner; do not bypass a denial.

findings.name: AI extraction readability
findings.evidence: TinyFish Fetch returned 156 characters (excerpt complete). The 100-character warning threshold is a heuristic, not an understanding/SEO guarantee. "Example Domain": not present in Fetch text. Excerpt: This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission. This is not a service; avoid relying on it for testing and monitoring purposes.
findings.impact: Text available to Fetch can be consumed by extraction tools; semantic understanding and visibility are not proven.
findings.fix: Keep primary content as accessible text. Compare the excerpt to the intended summary; ensure important headings/content are included without login or canvas-only rendering.

limits: Single page and bounded rendered snapshot only; length thresholds and scoring are heuristics.
No Google rankings, indexing status, traffic, backlinks, Lighthouse scores or Core Web Vitals measured.
Search presence/absence is one provider query observation, excluded from scoring; no causal ranking claim.
JSON-LD syntax/presence only, not schema.org validation, factual accuracy or rich-result eligibility.
Remote TinyFish Fetch independently resolves/follows redirects; DNS/redirect safety there is a provider trust boundary. Local requests are pinned; Browser routes validate but cannot pin remote DNS.
Browser GET-only filtering, request cap and settling deadline can limit rendering; inaccessible DOM checks stay not tested.
No optional link requests, authentication, interactive actions, writes or audited-site modifications.
